sections.heading: Two beginnings
sections.body: John 1:1 deliberately echoes Genesis 1:1. In Genesis, God **speaks** and creation appears. In John, that speech is personal: *the Word* who was with God. Read both verses side by side before moving on.

sections.heading: Three claims in one verse
sections.body:
Notice the progression: the Word **existed**, the Word was **with** God, the Word **was** God. Tap “the Word” to open G3056 and see where else λόγος appears.

Question: which of the three claims does the rest of the prologue develop most?

sections.heading: He pitched His tent
sections.body: The verb σκηνόω (G4637) comes from the word for a tent. Compare Exodus 40:34, where the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle. ==John sees that glory in a person.==

sections.heading: Made known
sections.body: ἐξηγέομαι (G1834) gives us the English word *exegesis*. The Son is the one who explains the Father. Compare Hebrews 1:1-3.
